primary_task: Before implementing a feature, classify the request (spike/bounded/architectural), explore project context, ask clarifying questions and get the human partner's approval of a design (in chat or as a written spec committed to docs/superpowers/specs/).

requirements.name: user conversation (clarifying questions and approval)
requirements.evidence: "Ask clarifying questions — one at a time" ; "Get approval — STOP and wait for an explicit yes"
requirements.basis: "ask_user": "ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation"

requirements.name: read project files
requirements.evidence: "Explore project context — check files, docs, recent commits"
requirements.basis: "read": "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)"

requirements.name: git
requirements.evidence: "Write design doc — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit" ; "check files, docs, recent commits"
requirements.basis: "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: ... build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, ..."

requirements.name: writing-plans skill
requirements.evidence: "Transition to implementation — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan" (architectural path, step 9)
requirements.basis: "skill": "load an installed Claude Code skill, list and search skills and plugins" (manifest does not say whether writing-plans is installed; check the skill list)

requirements.name: visual companion local server
requirements.evidence: "Offer the visual companion just-in-time — NOT upfront." ; "If they accept, start the server with `--open`" (optional)
requirements.basis: grants: "local_servers" (a server can run in the session, but the manifest does not say the user's browser can reach it or that the companion script is installed)

notes: Reading: the core deliverable is an approved design; the agent's own reasoning and writing need no requirement. Unknown: writing-plans skill availability (only the architectural path's last hand-off), and the optional visual companion (opening a browser tab via `--open` from a cloud session may not reach the user). The git commit is local and is not an external write; a push is not asked for.
